rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – Just Cause Eviction Requirements
rules.quote: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.summary: After 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy, a landlord cannot terminate a tenancy without just cause stated in a written notice.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to residential real property after tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied for 12 months (or 24 months if additional adult tenants added before 24 months). Exempt: transient hotels, nonprofit hospitals/religious facilities/care facilities, dormitories, owner-occupied properties sharing bathroom/kitchen, single-family owner-occupied residences renting ≤2 units, duplex with owner occupancy, certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes), alienable units with certain ownership structures (if proper notice given), deed-restricted affordable housing. Does not apply to homeowner of mobilehome.
rules.exemption_note: Housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years exempt (except mobilehomes). Single-family owner-occupied renting ≤2 units exempt. Duplex with owner occupancy exempt. Alienable units exempt if ownership not REIT/corporation/LLC with corporate member and proper notice given. Yields to local ordinances adopted by Sept 1, 2019 or later ordinances more protective than state law.
rules.penalty: Liable to tenant for actual damages, reasonable attorney's fees and costs, and up to three times actual damages if willful or with oppression, fraud, or malice; punitive damages available. Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel may seek injunctive relief. Failure to comply renders termination notice void.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Just Cause Evictions
rules.quote: For a tenancy for which just cause is required to terminate the tenancy under subdivision (a), if an owner of residential real property issues a termination notice based on a no-fault just cause described in paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), the owner shall, regardless of the tenant's income, at the owner's option, do one of the following: (A) Assist the tenant to relocate by providing a direct payment to the tenant as described in paragraph (3). (B) Waive in writing the payment of rent for the final month of the tenancy, prior to the rent becoming due.
rules.summary: When terminating a tenancy for no-fault just cause, the landlord must either pay relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, regardless of tenant income.
rules.effective_date_evidence: This section shall become operative on April 1, 2024.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to tenancies subject to just cause requirements under subdivision (a); same exemptions apply as main just cause provision.
rules.exemption_note: Same exemptions as main just cause provision. Amount credited against other relocation assistance required by other law.
rules.penalty: Failure to strictly comply renders notice of termination void. If tenant fails to vacate after notice expires, relocation assistance or rent waiver is recoverable as damages in action to recover possession.
